fr:title.text: Linear Residual ⟜ as Brzozowski Derivative

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Linear Residual ⟜ as Brzozowski Derivative

fr:mainmatter.html:p: In Grammar.LinearFunction.Base, the right residual is (A ⟜ B) w = ∀ (w' : String) → B w' → A (w' ++ w). Reading this at a single-character grammar char c we get
(G ⟜ char c) w = ∀ w' → (char c) w' → G (w' ++ w) ≅ G (c ∷ w),
i.e. the Brzozowski derivative of G by c, up to the canonical iso char c · w ≅ c ∷ w for singleton matches.

So the calculus already has a semantic notion of derivative as a type constructor, not just as an operation on descriptions. The syntactic derivative δ c G should then denote exactly ⟦ G ⟧cfg ⟜ char c, and the Brzozowski adjointness c · G ≅ δ c G is an instance of the tensor/residual adjunction char c · G ⊢ H ⟺ G ⊢ H ⟜ char c.
Why this matters for the plan:

html:ul.html:li: It grounds δ in the calculus rather than treating it as an external device: δ c G = G ⟜ char c already has the right type.
It means the parser's recursive structure can be phrased internally as currying over char c · - / uncurrying over - ⟜ char c, without leaving the calculus.
It suggests CFGDesc may not need ⟜ as a primitive — the operator can live outside the description as long as we can compute δ on descriptions and prove ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg ≅ ⟦ G ⟧cfg ⟜ char c.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Open question: for grammars with nullable residuals the adjunction interacts with the nullability gating in δ c (G · H); make sure the semantic direction of the iso stays available in both cases. This is tracked in risks.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Sketch: the CFG derivative parser internal to LambekD

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Feasibility sketch for building the inductive derivative parser inside Lambek^{D} in Agda. The claim: it is definable and provable by combining the regex \delta + soundness on the brzozowski branch with \rhd /lob on the box branch; the one design decision is to put the guard in the datatype, and the one genuine risk is refl-time computation. Signatures below are schematic — proofs are holes, never postulates.

fr:title.text: Datatype: guard as a structural invariant

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Datatype: guard as a structural invariant

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The naive recursion δ c (var X) = δ c (def X) does not pass Agda's termination checker — def X is not a subterm and the keystone short-circuit is semantic. So encode the guard structurally, Greibach-style: a nonterminal is its finite list of guarded clauses ⌈c⌉ ⊗ tail.
fr:mainmatter.html:pre:
NT : Type -- finite context of nonterminals (e.g. Fin n)
data CFGDesc : Type where ⟨I⟩ ⟨⊥⟩ : CFGDesc -- ε , empty lit : ⟨ Alphabet ⟩ → CFGDesc -- ⌈c⌉ var : NT → CFGDesc -- nonterminal leaf _⊗_ _⊕_ : CFGDesc → CFGDesc → CFGDesc
record Production : Type where -- one nonterminal's productions field nullable : Bool -- is ε accepted? clauses : List (Alphabet × CFGDesc) -- guarded: (leading char , tail)
def : NT → Production -- the grammar = a table of productions
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The invariant "every var occurs behind a consumed terminal" is now unforgeable: a nonterminal reaches you only via a clauses entry, whose head is a literal. Unguarded grammars are not expressible.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Nullability and derivative: both structural, Agda-accepted

δ : Alphabet → CFGDesc → CFGDesc δ c ⟨I⟩ = ⟨⊥⟩ δ c ⟨⊥⟩ = ⟨⊥⟩ δ c (lit c′) = if c == c′ then ⟨I⟩ else ⟨⊥⟩ δ c (A ⊕ B) = δ c A ⊕ δ c B δ c (A ⊗ B) = δ c A ⊗ B ⊕ (if ν? fr:title.text: The real risk: does it compute?

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The real risk: does it compute?

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Type-checking and proofs are the easy direction. Reducing parse dyck "aabb" by refl is the wall, and the constraints are known:

html:ul.html:li: lob reduces by refl only in Eq-world — the well-founded order must be Eq-valued or löbWF sticks under transp (reference: the Eq-vs-transp Löb issue).
Tensors must be SplittingEq from the start, or the hcomp/path-Splittings blowup that stalled witness evaluation returns.
Derivative descriptions grow; compaction (generic \bot /I unit rewrites) is optional for correctness but may be load-bearing for computation.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Empirically Dyck-style refl-evaluation was made tractable this way, while regex/greedy parsers did not terminate — so Dyck at refl is the first target; a general CFGDesc interpreter that computes is the open question, not a definability one.

fr:title.text: Syntactic derivatives as an inductive CFG→CFG operation

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Syntactic derivatives as an inductive CFG→CFG operation

fr:mainmatter.html:p: To parse without solving for the reachable states yourself, present grammars as a syntax and define \delta _c once, structurally, as a map on that syntax — a total CFGDesc → CFGDesc operation. This spells out the inductive construction sketched in sss-00A6: what the datatype is, why \delta _c is total on it, and why the recursion case does not diverge. It is the concrete bridge from CFGDesc to the generic Löb parser.

fr:title.text: The datatype

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The datatype

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Fix a finite context \Gamma of nonterminals. A CFGDesc Γ is built from

html:ul.html:li: var X for X \in \Gamma — a nonterminal leaf;
I (the \varepsilon grammar), ⊥ (empty), ⌈c⌉ (a literal);
A ⊗ B (concatenation) and A ⊕ B (alternation).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A grammar equips each X \in \Gamma with a production def X : CFGDesc Γ, subject to the guard: in every def X, each var Y occurs under some ⌈c⌉ ⊗ (−) (no nonterminal is reachable without first consuming a terminal). This is the \rhd -guard at the level of descriptions. Dyck is def D = I ⊕ ⌈a⌉ ⊗ var D ⊗ ⌈b⌉ ⊗ var D.

fr:title.text: Nullability, inductively

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Nullability, inductively

fr:mainmatter.html:p: ν? : CFGDesc Γ → Bool is structural:

html:ul.html:li: ν? ⊥ = false, ν? I = true, ν? ⌈c⌉ = false;
ν? (A ⊕ B) = ν? A ∨ ν? B;
ν? (A ⊗ B) = ν? A ∧ ν? B;
ν? (var X) = ν? (def X).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The last clause looks circular but is not, because of the guard: inside def X every var Y sits under a ⌈c⌉ ⊗ (−), and ν? (⌈c⌉ ⊗ −) = false ∧ − = false short-circuits before any ν? (var Y) is consulted. So a nonterminal's nullability depends only on its terminal-free (base) clauses — a finite, non-recursive table. This is the "nullability collapses" half of the keystone.

fr:title.text: The derivative, inductively

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The derivative, inductively

fr:mainmatter.html:p: δ c : CFGDesc Γ → CFGDesc Γ — note the same \Gamma : the residual carries the original nonterminals as leaves. On the description formers it is the classical Brzozowski recursion:

html:ul.html:li: δ c ⊥ = ⊥, δ c I = ⊥;
δ c ⌈c'⌉ = I if c' = c, else ⊥;
δ c (A ⊕ B) = δ c A ⊕ δ c B;
δ c (A ⊗ B) = δ c A ⊗ B ⊕ (if ν? A then δ c B else ⊥).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The \otimes -clause is the whole game, and it must short- circuit: when ν? A = false, the second summand is ⊥ and δ c B is not computed. The nonterminal case unfolds once:

html:ul.html:li: δ c (var X) = δ c (def X).

fr:title.text: Why this terminates and stays a CFG

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Why this terminates and stays a CFG

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Totality / structurality. The only non-structural clause is δ c (var X) = δ c (def X), and it fires at most once per nonterminal per step: differentiating def X, every var Y it contains sits behind a guard ⌈c'⌉ ⊗ (−), so the \otimes -clause short-circuits (ν? ⌈c'⌉ = false) and δ c (var Y) is never reached. Hence no nested δ c (var −) call, no divergence — one unfold and a finite structural pass. This is exactly the keystone lemma: the guard keeps the self-differentiation gate shut, so δ is total by structural recursion with no auxiliary fixed point.

Closure. δ c G is again a CFGDesc Γ over the same nonterminals — the residual mentions var X, never a differentiated nonterminal. So CFGDesc Γ is closed under δ, and iterating \delta stays in the syntax. The description grows (the \otimes - clause copies B), which is the unbounded state space showing up as unbounded term size; keeping it small is compaction — generic \bot /I-unit rewrites, an optimization, decoupled from totality.

Dyck check. δ a (var D) = δ a (def D) = δ a I ⊕ δ a (⌈a⌉ ⊗ (D ⊗ ⌈b⌉ ⊗ D)). The literal clause gives I ⊗ (D ⊗ ⌈b⌉ ⊗ D); the tail branch ν? ⌈a⌉ · δ a (…) short-circuits to ⊥ (never touching δ a (var D)). Result: D ⊗ ⌈b⌉ ⊗ D. Symmetrically δ b (var D) = ⊥. The stack states are whatever these iterates produce — the construction never names them.

fr:title.text: Feeding the parser

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Feeding the parser

fr:mainmatter.html:p: With ν? and δ as total structural maps on CFGDesc Γ, the generic Löb parser

is a single term — at ε answer ν? G, at c ∷ w recurse (under \rhd ) at δ c G — instantiated at the Dyck description. The soundness datum is the semantic bridge ⟦ δ c G ⟧ ≅ ⟦ G ⟧ ⟜ ⌈c⌉ of sss-00A7, proved once by induction on CFGDesc alongside this definition, so parse trees ride the isos. This is phases 1–3 of the plan made explicit.

fr:title.text: The internal automaton

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The internal automaton

fr:mainmatter.html:p: An automaton is a grammar A read as a \rhd -guarded coalgebra of internal Brzozowski shape: an output \nu A and, per letter c, a transition to the derivative \delta _c A. Both are internal — the transition is the linear residual \delta _c A (right adjoint of \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes {\mathopen {}\left (-\right )\mathclose {}}; A ⟜ char c of sss-00A7), an operation of the calculus, not a map on a state set outside it.
The coalgebra law is the first-character decomposition, an internal isomorphism

It is guarded: \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes {\mathopen {}\left (-\right )\mathclose {}} factors through \rhd (sss-00EX), so each recursive occurrence \delta _c A sits under a \rhd . Every grammar carries this canonically — the derivative is the transition — so "automaton" is not extra data but the internal reading of a grammar as its own Brzozowski coalgebra.

fr:title.text: The state space is internal, and Löb runs it without enumerating it

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The state space is internal, and Löb runs it without enumerating it

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Reading w moves A to the iterated residual \delta _w A; the reachable states are these residuals, an internal family. For non-regular A it is not finitely presented (e.g. Dyck's unbounded stack), but that never obstructs a parse: the run is a Löb fixed point visiting only the states along the input, generating each transition \delta _c on demand. There is nothing to enumerate.

One internal caveat on variance. The decomposition above exhibits A as an algebra-shaped fixed point through a free iso. The genuinely-extra coalgebra structure is \mathsf {next} : A \vdash \rhd A (suffix-closure), which is not free (sss-00BD) — via \lhd \dashv \rhd it is equivalently \lhd A \vdash A, "every derivative maps back into A". The run needs neither \mathsf {next} nor any chosen coalgebra as extra data — only \nu and \delta — but the gap is why observing (a \rhd - coalgebra) and building (a Löb fixed point) are distinct internal capabilities, related by \lhd \dashv \rhd rather than equal.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The derivative parser, the automaton, and Löb — end to end

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A precise, self-contained account of three things the derivative-parser plan keeps circling, and how they fit together: (1) what the derivative parser is (sss-00F2), (2) what an automaton is here (sss-00F3), and (3) how to implement automaton parsers by Löb induction (sss-00F4). fr:title.text: The derivative parser is the run

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The derivative parser is the run

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Fix the internal answer grammar \mathrm {Ans}_G := G \oplus \neg G (decide-and-produce; the parse forest is the left injection). It carries two free, internal properties (setup in sss-00F1):

html:ul.html:li: nullability \nu ?\,G, a decision of \nu G: the map that at \varepsilon picks an inhabitant of \mathrm {Ans}_G. Finite and structural on the guarded fragment.
derivative commutes \delta _c \mathrm {Ans}_G \;\cong \; \mathrm {Ans}_{\delta _c G}, since \delta _c is a right adjoint (preserves \oplus ) and commutes with \neg . Definitional.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The derivative parser of G is the entailment

read off the guarded first-character decomposition \top \;\cong \; I \;\oplus \; \bigoplus _c \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes \rhd \top : at the I summand answer \nu ?\,G; at the \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes \rhd \top summand consume c and, later, run \mathsf {parse}_{\delta _c G}, transporting the result along \delta _c \mathrm {Ans}_G \cong \mathrm {Ans}_{\delta _c G}. So the parser walks the input, replacing G by \delta _c G at each character, and answers with \nu ? at the end — the automaton run, closed by Löb.

Why it is a run, not a single-carrier fold. Unfolding a \Phi -algebra on a grammar A, for \Phi X = I \oplus \bigoplus _c \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes X (via the coproduct and \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes {\mathopen {}\left (-\right )\mathclose {}}\dashv \delta _c), yields a base I \vdash A plus prepend maps A \vdash \delta _c A. For A = \mathrm {Ans}_G the required prepend \mathrm {Ans}_G \vdash \mathrm {Ans}_{\delta _c G} does not exist — deciding G does not decide \delta _c G. The run instead transports the answer the other way, \delta _c\mathrm {Ans}_G \cong \mathrm {Ans}_{\delta _c G}, moving the grammar G \rightsquigarrow \delta _c G under the guard. So it is not a catamorphism into a fixed carrier; it is the guarded unfolding of sss-00F4.

Existence and uniqueness are Löb's, internal to the calculus: the recursive occurrence sits under \rhd , so \mathsf {parse}_G is the unique entailment satisfying the two clauses above. Uniqueness is the correctness statement — the c2a / family-hylomorphism reading of sss-00A9/sss-00F0.

fr:title.text: Automaton parsers via Löb

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Automaton parsers via Löb

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The derivative parser is a guarded fixed point: recurse inside the calculus, the recursive call guarded by \rhd because it sits behind a consumed character. This is the entire implementation — there is no separate termination argument.

Package the parser as one grammar: the internal indexed product P := \mathchoice {\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (G\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (G\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (G\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (G\right )\mathclose {}}}}\mathrm {Ans}_G over the type of grammars (an internal \Pi , exactly the contextual-Löb setting of sss-00EX, sss-00BZ). A recursive call at \delta _c G sits behind a consumed c, hence under \rhd , so it is available in \rhd P.

step : ▷ P ⊢ P step G = case-of-input I → ν? G -- ε: no ▷ obligation, answer nullability ⌈c⌉ ⊗ ▷P → later (λ rec → transport (rec (δ c G))) -- consumed c ⟹ recursive call is under ▷ -- δc (Ans G) ≅ Ans (δc G) transports the answer back

html:ul.html:li: The guard is discharged by consumption. The recursive occurrence is at \delta _c G behind a consumed c, and \lceil {c}\rceil \otimes {\mathopen {}\left (-\right )\mathclose {}} factors through \rhd (sss-00EX) — the character you read is the step of \rhd , so the call lands in \rhd P and no separate termination argument is needed.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Recursive grammars slot in the same way. Dyck over the bracket letters a, b, D = I \oplus \texttt {"}a\texttt {"}\otimes D \otimes \texttt {"}b\texttt {"}\otimes D, is itself \mathsf {lob}\,F for guarded F (sss-00AC, sss-00EX); running the parser on it needs \delta _c D, which the keystone supplies by a single unfold of F (a finite residual over D, no auxiliary fixed point), and \nu ?\,D by the same guard. So both the grammar and its parser are guarded fixed points, and the guard is paid for, once, by reading a character.

Summary. The automaton is a grammar with {\mathopen {}\left (\nu ,\ \delta \right )\mathclose {}} (sss-00F3); the derivative parser is its run (sss-00F2); Löb is what writes both the recursive grammars and the run as guarded fixed points, entirely inside the calculus. The general story of sss-00A9/sss-00F0 reads the same run as a c2a-morphism / family hylomorphism with correctness = uniqueness.

fr:title.text: The pipeline

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The pipeline

fr:mainmatter.html:p: To parse a grammar G (possibly recursively defined):

html:ol.html:li: Define G by guarded fixed point — G = \mathsf {lob}\,F for guarded F (sss-00EX, sss-00AC).
Derive \delta _c G total, by one unfold of F (keystone); \nu ?\,G decidable by the same guard.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Correctness is not a separate proof: each derivative step is an equality of answer types, so \mathsf {parse} is the unique family satisfying its two defining equations — the uniqueness half of the c2a-morphism reading, sharpened by locally-contractive parsing.

fr:title.text: Parsing with derivatives for a locally contractive family of grammars

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Parsing with derivatives for a locally contractive family of grammars

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Goal. Give a single, generic parser — producing parse trees, not an accept/reject bit — that works for any locally contractive endofunctor F on families of grammars, taking local-contractivity of F as the only hypothesis. In the intrinsic setting a grammar is its family of parse trees: a parse of w in G is an element of ⟦G⟧ w. So the parser must produce inhabitants of ⟦G*⟧ w (a whole forest, for ambiguous G), and the derivative must carry those inhabitants. This is the confluence of the derivative cluster with the local-contractivity / hylomorphism machinery: a recursive grammar family is the unique fixed point of a locally contractive functor, and its parser is the family hylomorphism that transports parse trees through the chain of derivative isomorphisms.

Conventions as in sss-00EZ, but read proof-relevantly: ε is the empty-string grammar, ⊥ the empty grammar, · concatenation, ⊕ alternation, char a a literal, δ c the derivative. Write ν G for the ε-part grammar of G — the subgrammar carrying exactly G's empty-string parses, (ν G) ε = G ε and ⊥ elsewhere. This is a grammar (it holds parse trees), not a Boolean; the recognizer's ν? is only its collapse to inhabited-or-not.

fr:title.text: Setup: a family of grammars as the fixed point of a contractive functor

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Setup: a family of grammars as the fixed point of a contractive functor

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Grammars are presheaves over (\stringg , \sqsubseteq ), \sqsubseteq the suffix order. A family of grammars is G : I \to \mathbf {Gr} for an index type I (the nonterminals / reachable derivative states). The later modality \rhd is front-consuming, (\rhd G)\,w = \prod _{u \sqsubset w} G\,u.

A functor F : \mathbf {Gr}^I \to \mathbf {Gr}^I is locally contractive when it factors through \rhd fibrewise — F(G)_i\,w depends on G only at proper suffixes of w. By the combinator calculus this is automatic when F is built from constants, the one-step guards char a · (−), and ⊕ / · / ⊗ positionwise: the grammar functor language, i.e. the string-ranked containers. Local contractivity gives a unique fixed point G^\ast = \mu F \cong F(G^\ast ) (Löb / Banach) — the recursive grammar family we parse. "F locally contractive" replaces every earlier guardedness device.

fr:title.text: Step 1 — the derivative is a proof-relevant iso; parsing transports trees

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Step 1 — the derivative is a proof-relevant iso; parsing transports trees

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Every grammar decomposes by first character, as a grammar isomorphism that carries parse trees:
G ≅ ν G ⊕ ⊕[c] char c · δ c G.
A parse of ε lands in ν G; a parse of c ∷ w splits as "the character c, then a parse of δ c G on w". The engine of the whole construction is the derivative iso
deriv : char c · G ≅ δ c G , equivalently (δ c G) w ≅ G (c ∷ w) ,
which is proof-relevant both ways: deriv pushes a "c-then-G" tree into a δ c G tree, and deriv⁻¹ recovers it. This is the ⟜-as-derivative content, not a decision.

The guard behaves as the character-indexed \rhd _c of sss-00AC, and the derivative is its force: from the adjunction {\mathopen {}\left (\char c \cdot -\right )\mathclose {}} \dashv \delta c of sss-00EY,

html:p.html:code: δ c (char c · G) = δ c(char c) · G ⊕ ν(char c) · δ c G = ε · G ⊕ ⊥ = G

fr:mainmatter.html:p: is the unit iso — differentiating past the guard by its own character returns the guarded grammar, with its parse tree intact (the leading c stripped). δ c' (char c · G) = ⊥ for c' ≠ c.

fr:title.text: Step 2 — functor-level keystone: local contractivity makes δ total

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Step 2 — functor-level keystone: local contractivity makes δ total

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Lemma. If F is locally contractive then, for every family G, δ c (F G) depends on G but not on δ c G.

Proof. Push δ c through F by the (proof-relevant) chain rule δ c (A · B) = δ c A · B ⊕ ν A · δ c B. Every recursive occurrence of G sits under a guard char a · (⋯G⋯) — that is what local contractivity is. The branch that would recurse toward δ c G is ν(char a) · δ c(⋯G⋯), and ν(char a) = ⊥ (a literal has no empty parse) kills it; the other branch keeps (⋯G⋯), hence G, undifferentiated. So δ c(F G) never contains δ c G. ∎

Consequence. On the fixed point δ c G^\ast = δ c(F G^\ast ) is a residual over G^\ast (undifferentiated) and derivatives of the non-recursive parts — computed by one unfolding of F, no circular δ c G^\ast . Hence δ c is total on the whole reachable derivative family, generically, for any locally contractive F. This promotes the sss-00EZ keystone from a syntactic argument to a corollary of local contractivity — and because δ is proof-relevant, it transports parse trees while it goes.

fr:title.text: Step 3 — the parser as a family hylomorphism

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Step 3 — the parser as a family hylomorphism

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The parser produces the parse forest parse G* w : ⟦G*⟧ w by walking the derivative isos down to ε and reshaping back:

html:p.html:code: parse G* ε = the ε-parses of G* ( inhabitants of (ν G*) ε )
parse G* (c ∷ w) = deriv⁻¹ (parse (δ c G*) w)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: where parse (δ c G*) w : (δ c G*) w reshapes along (δ c G*) w ≅ G* (c ∷ w) into a parse of the full string. Nothing here is Boolean: each step transports an actual tree, and the ε-base returns the set of empty-string parse trees (many, for ambiguous G*), so the output is the full parse forest.

This is exactly a HyloFam: the coalgebra unfolds the input against the derivative dynamics δ (the contractive strength, sss-00EP/sss-00EO; the mate G\circ H\circ U is locally contractive), and the algebra folds parse trees back up through deriv⁻¹; the carrier is the parse family ⟦G*⟧. Totality combines (i) each δ c step total (Step 2) with (ii) structural recursion on the input, terminating in |w| steps. The reachable derivative family is infinite for non-regular G^\ast , but a single parse visits only the length-|w| path — the hylo never materialises the state space.

fr:title.text: Step 4 — soundness and completeness are automatic: the parser is an iso

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Step 4 — soundness and completeness are automatic: the parser is an iso

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The whole fold is the composite of proof-relevant derivative isos
⟦G*⟧ w = ⟦G*⟧ (c₁⋯cₙ) ≅ ⟦δ c₁ G*⟧ (c₂⋯cₙ) ≅ ⋯ ≅ ⟦δ_w G*⟧ ε ,

using G* ≅ F G* and the Step-2 identity to compute each step. So parse G* is not a recognizer whose correctness needs proving — it is this bijection computed. Soundness (every produced tree is a genuine parse) and completeness (every genuine parse is produced) hold by construction, because each deriv is an isomorphism; semantic actions ride along the isos untouched. The μ = ν coincidence for the guarded fixed point says G^\ast is at once the initial algebra (parse trees exist inductively) and the final coalgebra (they are exactly the language's parses), so "the parse forest" is unambiguous as an object.

fr:title.text: Worked example: a mutually recursive family

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Worked example: a mutually recursive family

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Take I = \{S, T\} and
F(G)_S = char a · G_T · char b ⊕ ε , F(G)_T = char c · G_S · char d ⊕ ε.
δ a S = ε · (T · char b) ⊕ ⊥ = T · char b , δ c T = S · char d , others ⊥.
Parsing acdb in S descends four derivative isos to an ε-parse and reshapes back to a parse tree:

html:p.html:code: S --a--> T · char b --c--> S · char d · char b --d--> char b --b--> ε

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The ε-parse at the end is the innermost S → ε; deriv⁻¹ applied four times rebuilds
S( a , T( c , S(ε) , d ) , b ) ,
i.e. the actual nested tree, not a yes. No fixed point was solved and only the four states on the path were touched.

fr:title.text: Where this lives

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Where this lives

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Admissible F = the local-contractivity combinators / grammar functor language; the generic parser is a ranked-container hylomorphism with the proof-relevant δ as its strength; the fixed point and its \mu =\nu character are sss-00EV. Derivative / ε-part / parser pieces are sss-00A6–sss-00A8, the derivative iso char c · G ≅ δ c G is sss-00A7, the adjunction {\mathopen {}\left (\char c \cdot -\right )\mathclose {}}\dashv \delta c is sss-00EY, and the syntactic shadow of Step 2 is sss-00EZ. Parsing with derivatives is not a bespoke algorithm — it is the tree-transporting family hylomorphism that every locally contractive grammar functor already carries.

fr:title.text: The guard makes δ total: derivative parsing for the guarded CFG fragment

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The guard makes δ total: derivative parsing for the guarded CFG fragment

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Claim. If we restrict parsing-with-derivatives to the guarded (productive) grammar fragment — the same well-formedness condition of sss-00AC that we already impose to make recursive grammar definitions meaningful — then the two things that make parsing-with-derivatives hard for general context-free grammars both disappear, and the derivative becomes an ordinary total, structurally-defined operation. This tree spells out why, because the reason is not obvious and is the whole basis for the feasibility claim.

Throughout, ε is the grammar matching only the empty string (the tensor unit), ⊥ the grammar matching nothing, · concatenation, ⊕ alternation, A* Kleene star, and char a the single-character grammar. δ c G is the syntactic derivative and ν? G the nullability gate (ν? G = ε if G accepts the empty string, else ⊥).

fr:title.text: Background: what parsing-with-derivatives does, and why general CFGs are hard

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Background: what parsing-with-derivatives does, and why general CFGs are hard

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The Brzozowski derivative δ c G is "G, assuming the first character c has already been read": it is a proof-relevant iso (δ c G) w ≅ G (c ∷ w) (sss-00A7), so it transports parse trees, not just acceptance. Parsing is then a fold over the input — one derivative per character — that at the end reads off the empty-string parse trees of the residual and reshapes them back through the derivative isos into a parse of the whole input (the full construction, and why it is a genuine tree-producing parser rather than a recognizer, is sss-00F0):

html:p.html:code: parse G (c ∷ w) = deriv⁻¹ (parse (δ c G) w)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Here ν? below is only the nullability gate inside δ's definition (does the empty-string part exist), not the output.
The derivative is computed by pushing δ c through the grammar structure. The two rules that recurse into subgrammars are the ones to watch:

html:p.html:code: δ c (A ⊕ B) = δ c A ⊕ δ c B
δ c (A · B) = δ c A · B ⊕ ν? A · δ c B

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The product rule is the subtle one. Differentiating a concatenation A · B has two cases: either the first character came from A (giving δ c A · B), or A could match the empty string and the first character came from B (giving δ c B, but only if A is nullable — hence the ν? A gate).
Where general CFGs break. For a recursive grammar the derivative can refer back to itself. Take the left-recursive E = (E · char a) ⊕ char b. Differentiating:

html:p.html:code: δ a E = δ a (E · char a) ⊕ δ a (char b) = (δ a E · char a ⊕ ν? E · δ a (char a)) ⊕ ⊥

fr:mainmatter.html:p: which is an equation defining δ a E in terms of δ a E. There is no structural computation here: δ a E can only be obtained as the least fixed point of that equation. This is exactly why the classical functional-pearl implementation (Might–Darais–Spiewak 2011) needs laziness, observable sharing, and memoized fixed points — and why nullability there is also a least-fixed-point computation. Both difficulties come from a nonterminal being reachable by δ without any character being consumed first.

fr:title.text: The keystone: guardedness cuts every self-differentiation branch

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The keystone: guardedness cuts every self-differentiation branch

fr:mainmatter.html:p: A grammar is guarded when, in every production, each nonterminal occurrence is preceded by a non-nullable prefix — you cannot reach the nonterminal without first consuming at least one terminal. (E above is not guarded: its recursive E is the leading factor, preceded by nothing.)

Keystone Lemma. On the guarded fragment, δ c is a total function definable by structural recursion, computed with one unfolding of each fixed point and no auxiliary fixed point or memoization; moreover it sends guarded grammars to guarded grammars.

Why. The only way δ c fails to terminate structurally is if computing δ c X for a nonterminal X requires computing δ c X again — the cyclic equation we saw for E. That happens iff δ c can descend to a differentiated occurrence of X, i.e. iff X is reachable in the production body without passing a consuming prefix. Guardedness forbids exactly this. Consider where a guarded X sits: behind a non-nullable prefix A, as A · (⋯X⋯). The product rule splits differentiation of A · (⋯X⋯) into two branches:

html:ul.html:li: δ c A · (⋯X⋯) — keeps the X-containing tail unchanged, so X is carried along as an undifferentiated leaf; and
ν? A · δ c (⋯X⋯) — the branch that would recurse toward δ c X, but A is non-nullable, so ν? A = ⊥ and this whole branch is ⊥.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: So δ c reaches every nonterminal only through the first branch, as a leaf it does not differentiate. Concretely, computing δ c X for a guarded X unfolds X's body once and makes a single structural pass, treating every nonterminal in the body (recursive or not) as an opaque leaf, because each is guarded and its ν?-gate is ⊥. The pass therefore calls δ c on no nonterminal at all — it cannot diverge, and it cannot form a cycle (even a mutual one). The output is a finite expression over the original nonterminals. ∎

The contrast with E: for E the recursive occurrence has an empty (hence nullable) prefix, so the ν? A gate is ε rather than ⊥, the second branch survives, and δ a E is forced to recurse into δ a E. The guard is precisely the syntactic condition that keeps that gate shut.

fr:title.text: Worked example: aⁿbⁿ (guarded, not regular)

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Worked example: aⁿbⁿ (guarded, not regular)

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Let S = (char a · S · char b) ⊕ ε. The recursive S is guarded — it sits behind the non-nullable char a. First derivative:

html:p.html:code: δ a S = δ a (char a · (S · char b)) ⊕ δ a ε
= [ δ a (char a) · (S · char b) ⊕ ν?(char a) · δ a (S · char b) ] ⊕ ⊥
= [ ε · (S · char b) ⊕ ⊥ · δ a (S · char b) ] ⊕ ⊥

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Notice the second branch ν?(char a) · δ a (S · char b) became ⊥ because ν?(char a) = ⊥. This is the gate closing: we never had to compute δ a (S · char b), so the computation of δ a S terminates in one unfold, and the result S · char b carries the original S undifferentiated.
Now a residual like S · char b does have S as its leading factor, so its own derivative genuinely calls δ a S:

html:p.html:code: δ a (S · char b) = δ a S · char b ⊕ ν? S · δ a (char b) = (S · char b) · char b ⊕ (ε · ⊥) = S · char b · char b

fr:mainmatter.html:p: But δ a S here is just the terminating one-unfold computation above (= S · char b), so there is no infinite regress — only a finite chain of residuals S, S · char b, S · char b · char b, …, each a finite expression over the original S. The state space is infinite (this grammar is not regular), but see below: that never matters for a single parse.

fr:title.text: Nullability collapses for the same reason

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Nullability collapses for the same reason

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For general CFGs, ν? is itself a least fixed point: whether a nonterminal is nullable can depend recursively on whether it is nullable. The guard removes this too, by the identical mechanism. A guarded recursive occurrence sits behind a non-nullable prefix, and
ν?(char a · X) = ν?(char a) · ν? X = ⊥ · ν? X = ⊥, for any X.

So a production containing a guarded recursive occurrence is non-nullable outright, regardless of the occurrence's own nullability — the recursive dependency is severed. Nullability of μX. F is then determined entirely by the non-recursive (base) alternatives of F, computable by structural recursion with no iteration to a fixed point. For aⁿbⁿ:
ν? S = ν?(char a · S · char b) ⊕ ν? ε = ⊥ ⊕ ε = ε (nullable, via the ε branch), computed without ever consulting ν? S.
This is why sss-00A5 is clean on the guarded fragment, and the same ν?-computation doubles as the check that a grammar really is guarded.

fr:title.text: What does not collapse — and why it is harmless

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: What does not collapse — and why it is harmless

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Infinitely many derivatives. As the aⁿbⁿ example shows, a guarded (indeed any non-regular) grammar has infinitely many distinct derivative states, so there is no finite derivative automaton to precompute. This sounds alarming but is irrelevant to actually parsing: parsing a fixed input w takes exactly |w| derivative steps, each a total finite operation, and the parser is structurally recursive on the input list. You never enumerate the state space; you only ever walk one path of length |w| through it. (This is the same observation sss-00A6 makes as "infinite but regular-in-the-right-sense".)

Description blow-up. The product rule duplicates subgrammars — δ c (A · B) mentions B in one branch and δ c B in the other — so a naively-represented residual can grow exponentially in |w|. The remedy is compaction: algebraic simplification after each step (⊥ · x = ⊥, ε · x = x, x ⊕ ⊥ = x, and sharing of common nonterminals). The essential point for us is that compaction is an optimization, not a correctness requirement: a total, correct parser exists without it (each step is already total), so compaction and its semantics-preservation proof can be added later, purely for performance. This is the one place where the general-CFG performance story (cubic only with compaction, per Adams–Hollenbeck–Might 2016) still applies — but it is decoupled from totality and correctness.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Deliverables

fr:mainmatter.html:p: With the keystone lemma in hand the remaining work is small and well-scoped:

html:ol.html:li: Totality and guard-preservation of δ — formalize the keystone lemma: on the guarded fragment δ c is total, structural, and maps guarded grammars to guarded grammars. This discharges the "μ is the part most likely to need care" flag of sss-00A6 and the corresponding risk; the care needed is precisely the ν?-gate argument above.

The parser as a fold / Löb fixed point — the length-recursion parser of sss-00A8, parse G (c ∷ w) = deriv⁻¹ (parse (δ c G) w), producing parse trees by reshaping along the derivative iso, optionally recast as the (Brz) Löb fixed point of sss-00EY / sss-00EX for a modality-native presentation (the guarded recursion is exactly what Löb discharges). Its output is the parse forest ⟦G⟧ w, per sss-00F0.

Soundness and completeness are automatic — the derivative commutation ⟦ δ c G ⟧ ≅ ⟦ G ⟧ ⟜ char c of sss-00A7 is a proof-relevant iso, so the fold is the bijection ⟦G⟧ w ≅ ⟦δ_w G⟧ ε; there is no separate correctness proof, and parse trees / semantic actions ride along the isos. Because δ is structural, no fixed-point / domain-theoretic reasoning is needed.
(Optional) Compaction with preservation — for performance only: prove each simplification rule is a grammar isomorphism, so parse trees / semantic actions are preserved.

fr:title.text: Precision: "guarded", not "non-left-recursive"

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Precision: "guarded", not "non-left-recursive"

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The exact restriction is the ▷-guard of sss-00AC: every self-reference under a non-nullable prefix. This is strictly stronger than "not directly left-recursive". Consider hidden left recursion, A = (B · A) ⊕ c with B nullable: A is not the syntactic leading factor, but because B can vanish, A is still reachable with no character consumed, so ν? B = ε keeps the dangerous branch open and δ c A again becomes cyclic. Guardedness rules this out too — it is about consumption, not syntactic position. So state the fragment as guarded / productive.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: ▷ as a Later Modality from Tiny Strings

fr:title.text: Strings are tiny

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Strings are tiny

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The amazing-right-adjoint construction goes through for any tiny object, not only single characters. In the grammar setting strings are tiny: an inhabited string is a finite product of literal grammars under \otimes , and \texttt {"}c\texttt {"} \otimes - preserves all colimits, so iterating gives a left adjoint \texttt {String}\, w \otimes - with both adjoints on the right.

Notation. fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The candidate ▷

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Define \rhd A \;:=\; \mathchoice {\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\textstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}{\scriptscriptstyle \And _{{\mathopen {}\left (w \in \texttt {String}^{+}\right )\mathclose {}}}}\sqrt [w]{A}. The indexing is by all non-empty strings simultaneously, so the modality is character-agnostic in the same sense as classical guarded type theory's ▷, while being grounded in concrete suffix-extraction at every non-empty depth.
Two design questions are baked into the definition.

html:ul.html:li: Side. We pick the left-handed \sqrt [w]{}, which encodes "any proper suffix"; the right-handed choice gives "any proper prefix". They are symmetric and either could serve. A genuinely two-sided ▷ encoding "any proper substring" is the natural next target — see TODOs below.

Why non-empty. Empty w would give \sqrt [\epsilon ]{A} \cong A, collapsing \rhd A \vdash A into a strict identity and killing Löb. Restricting to non-empty strings keeps the modality genuinely "later".

fr:title.text: What we want to verify

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: What we want to verify

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The candidate is only useful if it has the structural rules of a later modality. Three properties to check.

html:ol.html:li: Next. A canonical map \mathsf {next} : A \vdash \rhd A. fr:title.text: Later Operator ▶ as Internalised Guard

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Later Operator ▶ as Internalised Guard

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The plan is self-contained without any modalities: productivity is a side condition on CFGDesc, nullability is an external decision sss-00A5, and well-foundedness is operational recursion on length sss-00A8. A later operator ▶ would internalise each of these into the type system, making the same construction fall out of guarded fixpoint rather than a sequence of external theorems.
Two natural slots for ▶:

html:p.html:strong: 1. As the guard on μ in CFGDesc.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: The current productivity condition on CFGDesc ("every self-reference sits under a non-nullable prefix") is a bespoke later modality indexed by "must consume ≥1 char." First-class ▶ replaces the side condition with a syntactic requirement:

where F is any unconstrained CFGDesc-style functor. This is exactly the trade-up that the Grammar.SequentialUnambiguity.Nullable scaffolding already gestures at: ¬Nullable A is a proposition about a grammar; ▶ would be a grammar constructor.

The paper's guard functor (F ↓₀) X i = F (λ j → (j ≺ i) × X j) i is already a parameterised later modality: the parameter is the well-founded relation ≺, not a global clock. So the machinery in IntrinsicallyRecursiveCoalgs.lagda is morally a per-index ▶, and moving to a syntactic ▶ is just factoring that indexing into the type theory.

html:p.html:strong: 2. As the meaning of A ⟜ char c.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Recall from ⟜-as-derivative that
(A ⟜ char c) w = A (c ∷ w),

i.e. inhabiting A ⟜ char c requires being fed one character before producing an A. This is the defining behaviour of a later modality: availability delayed by one step, where "step" = "one character consumed."
Under this reading the Brzozowski identity char c · A ≅ δ c A becomes an applicativity law:
char c · (A ⟜ char c) ⊢ A (▶-apply)
and the derivative-based parser is a guarded fixpoint:

html:p.html:code: parse : μ self. (char? ⟜ ε ⊕ (Σ c. ▶ (parse (δ c G))))

fr:mainmatter.html:p: where the self-reference is guarded by ▶ ≡ (_ ⟜ char c), and the well-foundedness witness F-ε⁻¹ of c2a-morph is exactly the "take a later and cash it in" rule.

html:ul.html:li: Nullability becomes decidable by typing. ε ⊢ A iff A is ▶-free at the outer layer; no external decision needed.
Length-well-foundedness becomes automatic. Each ▶-unfold consumes exactly one character, so recursion depth ≤ input length by construction. sss-00A8's use of <-wellFounded disappears.

c2a-morph becomes guarded fixpoint. The paper's uniqueness theorem specialises to the Löb-style uniqueness of guarded fixpoints in the appropriate topos. Computational content is the same; meta-theory is cleaner.
Not on the critical path. The plan works without ▶; this tree is about a cleaner re-foundation, not a missing step.

Integration cost. Adding ▶ as a primitive means revisiting every grammar operation (tensor, residual, fixed points) to specify its interaction with ▶. Feasible, but a larger design commitment than "a few side conditions."

Which ▶? Classical guarded type theory's ▶ is character-agnostic (one "tick" per step). Ours is character-indexed (▶_c A = A ⟜ char c). The paper's (F ↓₀) sits in between — indexed by an abstract ≺. Whether to use a single ▶ or a character-indexed family is itself a design question.

html:ol.html:li: Prototype ▶ A as an alias for Σ c : Alphabet. A ⟜ char c (character-indexed form) inside the existing calculus, without new primitives.
Re-state nullability as a syntactic check on ▶-absence at the top of a description.
Re-derive c2a-morph for the single-step case and see whether the ▶-elimination rule does the work currently done by F-ε⁻¹.
Only then consider adding ▶ to CFGDesc as a primitive constructor (step 1 of sss-00A4).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Open: does a character-indexed ▶ compose into a single modality after applying the "erase the character" projection? That would bridge the specific (Brzozowski-style) and generic (Löb-style) readings.

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Risks and Open Questions — Derivative-Based CFG Parser

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Risks for the plan, ordered by how likely they are to cause rework.

html:ul.html:li: Productivity of μ in CFGDesc. The non-nullable-prefix condition is the natural guardedness criterion, but formalising it compositionally (so all constructors preserve it with reasonable evidence) is not obvious. A too-strict condition rules out Dyck; a too-loose one fails to give well-founded derivatives.

Derivative descriptions on μ. Unfolding under δ is the standard trick, but in a strongly-typed setting we have to show that the unfolded description is again a legal CFGDesc (productivity preserved). Might need to enrich CFGDesc with a rec or ν constructor that tracks the "unfolded state".

Nullability gate interacting with ⟜. The Brzozowski rule δ c (G · H) = δ c G · H ⊕ ν? G · δ c H uses classical disjunction. In Lambek we need the grammar-level iso c · (G · H) ≅ (c · G) · H + [G is ε-derivable] · (c · H); the second summand is zero when G is non-nullable. Check that the ⟜-as-derivative framing still composes cleanly through this case distinction.

c2a-morph at Type vs Set. The intrinsically-recursive paper is formalised in Set^I. Grammars in this project are String → Type. The constructions look generic over the universe, but there may be isSet obligations (or propositional-truncation issues) hidden in the uniqueness proof. See parser as c2a-morphism.

Infinite state space. For CFGs the reachable derivatives of a grammar are unbounded. We don't need finitely many descriptions, but we do need each derivative to be well-typed and computable. The danger is that our description type is not closed under δ — i.e., δ produces something outside CFGDesc. This has to be proven, not just asserted.

Cass's Automata.Deterministic.parseNatTrans is a natural transformation between the word functor and the trace functor — a genuine coalgebraic object — but it gives a DFA-shaped coalgebra that doesn't obviously subsume our Parser A B return type. We may need to compose their NT-style result with a decide step on the final state to recover A ⊕ B. Not blocking, but a loose end.

Constructive negation of CFG. ¬ ⟦ G ⟧cfg w is what Parser wants on the reject side, but in general the negation of a CFG membership predicate is not itself a CFG. We will be inhabiting a proof of non-membership, not a grammar. Worth confirming that the disjointness obligation disjoint A B is satisfied by this formulation.

fr:title.text: Parser by Well-Founded Recursion on String Length

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Parser by Well-Founded Recursion on String Length

fr:mainmatter.html:p: We want a generic parser
for every G : CFGDesc, where Parser A B (from Parser.Base) packages a splitting string ⊢ A ⊕ B with a disjointness witness disjoint A B.
Construction, by induction on input length:

html:ol.html:li: If the input is ε, answer by decidable nullability: G is nullable ⟹ inhabit ⟦ G ⟧cfg, otherwise inhabit the rejection side.

If the input is c ∷ w, recursively parse (δ c G) w via the syntactic derivative. Using ⟜ as derivative, a positive answer ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg w reshapes to ⟦ G ⟧cfg (c ∷ w); a negative answer ¬ ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg w lifts to ¬ ⟦ G ⟧cfg (c ∷ w).

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Well-foundedness: on each recursive call length w strictly decreases. The grammar may grow (derivatives of CFGs are unbounded), but the well-founded relation is on the input, not the state. This mirrors how GCD.<₂-wellFounded in the intrinsically-recursive paper is well-founded on proj₂ of the index, not on the full index.
Concretely, the recursion uses <-wellFounded on ℕ via Cubical.Induction.WellFounded (already imported by the project's dependency on agda-stdlib).

This tree defines the algorithm operationally. The next step, parser as c2a-morphism, reinterprets the same definition as a unique coalgebra-to-algebra morphism, so the correctness proof becomes a uniqueness argument rather than a direct induction.

fr:title.text: Syntactic Derivatives on CFGDesc

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Syntactic Derivatives on CFGDesc

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Given a character c : Alphabet and a description G : CFGDesc, define a description δ c G : CFGDesc and a morphism at the semantics
deriv c G : char c · ⟦ G ⟧cfg ⊢ ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg ,
together with an inverse deriv⁻¹ c G : ⟦ δ c G ⟧cfg ⊢ char c · ⟦ G ⟧cfg , so the pair witnesses the Brzozowski identity c · G ≅ δ c G inside grammar (not language) semantics.
Regex case is classical:

html:ul.html:li: δ c ε = ⊥;
δ c (char a) = if a ≟ c then ε else ⊥;
δ c (G · H) = (δ c G) · H ⊕ ν? G · δ c H, where ν? gates the second summand by nullability;
δ c (G ⊕ H) = δ c G ⊕ δ c H;
δ c (G *) = δ c G · G *.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: For μ we unfold once before deriving, using the productivity side condition to ensure the derivative terminates at the description level (the description does not grow under δ past a bounded residual form). This is the part most likely to need care — see risks.

CFG derivatives in general (Might, Darais, Spiewak 2011) form an infinite but regular-in-the-right-sense family; the reachable derivative states for a given G correspond to the states of a PDA for G. We do not need finitely many residuals; we only need each derivative to be well-typed and to decrease the string length we feed it.

For Dyck specifically, the derivative by LP moves us to a state "expecting one extra RP before completion", and iterating gives the unbounded stack. The state space is infinite; the per-string computation is still well-founded on input length, which is where well-founded recursion on length comes in.
